headline: GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,471 AS IRAN STRIKE DECLARED SHORT-LIVED — Counter-Intuitive Sept 3 Move Reveals Fed Rates Dominate Geopolitics; Silver Recovers To $66.39
snippet: Gold climbed to $4,471 per ounce on September 3, 2026, recovering from Wednesday's $4,336 low after President Trump declared the U.S.-Iran military strike 'very heavy' but assured it 'won't take too long' — a signal traders interpreted as a short-lived flare rather than a sustained escalation. The paradox is instructive: gold actually fell on September 2 as Iran military actions intensified, and only recovered today when war appeared to be winding down — revealing that gold markets are currently dominated by Federal Reserve rate expectations and short positioning, not geopolitical risk premium. With oil back near $100 per barrel from the Iran disruption, inflation expectations complicate the NFP calculus ahead of Friday's August payrolls report; silver recovered to $66.39 per ounce on the day.

headline: FARADAY COPPER DISCOVERS COPPER GIANT EAST — New Oxide Zone 300m From Flagship Deposit In Arizona; 4 Holes Define 48-100m Surface-Exposed Mineralization
snippet: Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX-V: FDY) announced September 3 the results of 23 Phase IV drill holes at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, discovering a previously unknown copper oxide zone named Copper Giant East approximately 300 metres east of the flagship Copper Giant deposit: four holes returned copper oxide mineralization over 48 to 100 metres of downhole length in a mineralised area exposed at surface. Near-surface oxide mineralization was intersected in 14 of 23 total holes across multiple target areas, expanding both oxide and sulphide zones with an updated mineral resource estimate planned for 2027. Near-surface copper oxide at a porphyry system exposed at surface simplifies heap-leach or SX-EW optionality studies — the profile that accelerates resource estimate development and attracts pre-feasibility study interest.

headline: BRIXTON METALS 12,386 g/t SILVER IN HALF-METRE AT COBALT ONTARIO — Hole 432 Returns 6,199 g/t Ag Over 1m; S6 South Zone Extended 50m; 155 Holes Drilled In 2026
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation released September 2 assay results from 33 drill holes at the Langis Silver Project in Cobalt, Ontario — the historic high-grade silver mining camp that hosted some of the world's richest native silver deposits. Best result hole LM-26-432 returned 1.00 metre at 6,199 g/t silver including 0.50 metre of 12,386 g/t silver from 116 metres depth, while LM-26-399 returned 41 metres at 79.2 g/t silver and LM-26-401 returned 2 metres at 447 g/t silver in the Shaft 6 West area. The 2026 campaign has now completed 155 holes totalling 33,858 metres, systematically expanding the S6-SE envelope 50 metres to the south. At silver above $65 per ounce, ultra-high-grade narrow vein systems like Langis carry exceptional revenue per vertical metre — the economic profile that supports high-margin underground mine scenarios at modest tonnage scales.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING SPINS FIRST DRILL AT ORION — New 350m x 300m Colombia Target Returns 7.43 g/t Au, 230 g/t Ag At Surface; Victory Porphyry-Breccia Follows Q4
snippet: Collective Mining Ltd. (TSX: CNL) announced September 3 that its newly defined Orion target at the Guayabales Project in Caldas, Colombia — located 1 kilometre east of the flagship Apollo system — has advanced to drill-ready status: systematic mapping defined a 350 by 300 metre mineralised footprint in argillic- and sericite-altered quartz diorite with stockwork gold-bearing veining; surface rock samples returned up to 7.43 g/t gold, 230 g/t silver, 0.26% copper, and 85 ppm molybdenum, and soil samples ran to 4.00 g/t Au. First drill holes commence this week. The Company is also planning Q4 drilling at the Victory target, where reinterpretation of historical data has defined new porphyry-breccia and precious metal drill targets. Systematic satellite target generation around a proven large-scale system is the discovery pattern that precedes step-change resource growth at multi-deposit gold camps.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER 49.2m AT 4.7% COPPER EQUIV AT ALASKA VMS — 3.05% Cu, 4.85% Zn, 21.88 g/t Ag Confirm South Wall High-Grade Core; Program Expanded To 12,250m
snippet: Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSX-V: VCU) reported September 3 that drill holes CMR26-199 and CMR26-201 at the Palmer Copper-Zinc VMS Project in Southeast Alaska returned 49.2 metres at 4.7% copper equivalent — comprising 3.05% copper, 4.85% zinc, 21.88 g/t silver, and 0.33 g/t gold — confirming continuity of the high-grade copper core within South Wall Zone 1 and extending the mineralised system downdip. The 2026 drill program was expanded from 10,000 to approximately 12,250 metres after these initial results; fifteen additional holes across the HG, AG, South Wall Zones 2-3 and Waterfall targets are expected from late September through November. High-grade VMS copper-zinc results with a confirmed multi-zone system and 22% program expansion confirm the operational momentum at one of Alaska's premier base metal exploration addresses.

headline: NORTH SHORE URANIUM HITS IN ALL 13 HOLES AT NEW MEXICO — 27ft At 0.30% eU3O8; All 21 Intercepts Below Water Table; ISR-Amenable Grants District Discovery
snippet: North Shore Uranium Ltd. (CVE: NSU) reported September 3 Phase 1 results from its inaugural drill program at the Rio Puerco Uranium Project in the Grants Uranium District of northwestern New Mexico: significant uranium mineralization was intersected in all 13 of 13 rotary drill holes across 9,274 feet (2,828 metres), with 21 individual uranium intercepts including best intersection RP-26-18-39 returning 27 feet at 0.30% eU3O8. Critically, all 21 uranium intercepts are located below the water table — the defining characteristic required for in-situ recovery economics without conventional mining capital. The Grants Uranium District hosted or hosts operations by Uranium One, Rio Tinto, and Cameco; a 100% Phase 1 hit rate in an ISR-amenable setting advances directly to resource definition drilling in Phase 2, targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: SIBANYE OKAYS MINES ON TWO CONTINENTS AS H1 PROFIT TRIPLES — $340M Mt Lyell Copper Tasmania + R6.2bn Burnstone Gold SA; HEPS +216%, Revenue +64% To R90bn
snippet: Sibanye-Stillwater (JSE/NYSE: SSW) reported September 2 that first-half 2026 headline earnings per share surged 216% to 601 cents on revenue of R90 billion (+64% year-over-year) and adjusted EBITDA more than doubling to R31.8 billion — strong enough for the board to simultaneously approve two major greenfield capital projects: Mt Lyell copper-gold in Tasmania, Australia ($340 million, 26,000 tonnes annual copper by 2032, first production 2029) and Burnstone underground gold in South Africa (R6.2 billion, 130,000 ounces annually at steady state, 2.7 million ounce reserve base, 25-year mine life). Mt Lyell is Sibanye's first-ever copper mining operation. Two new mines on two continents approved on the same day signals major-producer-level conviction in copper and gold price outlooks through the next capital cycle — the kind of commitment that historically precedes increased junior exploration funding across the same commodity space.

headline: STALLION URANIUM MAPS THREE NEW ATHABASCA TARGETS AT STONE ISLAND — Gravity-VTEM Integration At Moonlite Project Saskatchewan Expands Pre-Drill Pipeline
snippet: Stallion Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: STUD) reported September 3 that integration of its 2026 ground gravity and VTEM Plus airborne electromagnetic surveys at the Stone Island target within the Moonlite Project in the southwestern Athabasca Basin identified three new high-priority exploration target areas — A, B, and C — expanding the drill pipeline beyond the previously defined Coyote target. The southwestern Athabasca Basin has drawn escalating attention following Paladin Energy's Atlas discovery 3.5 kilometres from Triple R at Patterson Lake South; multi-geophysical target stacking of the kind Stallion describes is the technical framework used to define drill targets in the basin's deeply buried basement-hosted uranium systems. Drill targeting is the next step before the 2026-2027 winter drill season.

headline: LITHIUM +105% YEAR-OVER-YEAR AT 156,000 CNY/T BUT FELL 0.3% ON SEPT 2 — Battery Storage Boom Underpins Demand Floor As LIT ETF Softens And Miners Trade Mixed
snippet: Lithium carbonate fell 0.32% to 156,000 CNY per tonne on September 2, 2026, with the LIT ETF declining and lithium miners trading mixed — but the daily move obscures the structural recovery: lithium prices are up 11.43% over the past month and 105.51% versus the same period last year, as battery energy storage deployment absorbs supply that was depressing prices in 2024-2025. Argentina is producing approximately 34,000 tonnes annually and could become the world's third-largest lithium producer by 2027 on the back of 18 active projects; Chile's National Lithium Strategy is attracting private capital through public-private partnerships. For junior lithium explorers, the commodity's 105% year-over-year recovery sets a materially improved backdrop for resource definition spending and project financing discussions.

headline: 3 GOLD MINERS TO OWN IN SEPTEMBER 2026: NEWMONT, COEUR, AND THE ROYALTY PLAY — Analysts ID Producers Generating Record Free Cash Flow At $4,400+ Gold
snippet: A September 3 analysis identifies three gold mining stocks positioned for outsized gains in the current cycle: Newmont Corporation, with flagship operations at NGM, Boddington, Peñasquito, and Yanacocha generating approximately US$13.9 billion in annual revenue; Coeur Mining, a North American gold-silver producer at Palmarejo, Rochester, and Las Chispas posting record revenue with 26.8% margins and a new dividend and buyback program; and royalty and streaming companies offering leveraged gold exposure without operational dilution. The overarching case: gold and silver mining equities remain priced well below comparable-margin industrials on a P/E basis despite generating record free cash flow at $4,400+ gold — a valuation dislocation the authors argue corrects sharply when the Fed pause trade materialises.
